title: Traffic light
summary: CSS art: a rounded housing with three stacked lamps, the green one glowing, on a pole.
brief: Draw a traffic light, centred horizontally in the street. The housing is 80px wide with 16px of padding above and below the lamps and 20px rounded corners.
The three lamps are 48px circles stacked vertically, centred, 12px apart. Red and amber are switched off: 30% opacity. Green is on: full colour with a glow (0 0 24px 6px in rgb(34 197 94 / 0.7)).
Under the housing, a 16 × 120px pole, also centred.
hints: The empty lamps and pole need a width and height before you can see them. A circle is a square with border-radius: 50%.

Stack the lamps with display: flex and flex-direction: column on .light; gap spaces them and align-items: center centres them. To centre the housing and pole in the street, make .street a grid with justify-items: center.
Dim two lamps in one rule: .red, .amber { opacity: 0.3; }. The glow is box-shadow: 0 0 24px 6px rgb(34 197 94 / 0.7) on .green.
solutionNotes: A column flex container does the stacking: gap spaces the lamps and align-items: center lines them up in the middle of the 80px housing. The street is a one-column grid, and justify-items: center centres both the housing and the pole under it. "Off" is just opacity, and "on" is a coloured box-shadow with blur and spread, which glows without changing the lamp’s size or moving anything.
